name: Interactive project globe
cadet: A 3D globe shows every project where it was built. Spin it, tap a glowing pin, and a card pops up with the photo and a link to the case study.
why: Visitors see the studio's reach in one second, before reading a word.
engineer: A factory function creates an independent [[Three.js]] globe per wrapper, so the hero and the teaser can coexist. Pins are read from hidden [[CMS]] items via data attributes (lat, lng, city, slug). Raycasting on invisible hitboxes handles hover and tap; nearby pins group into clusters.

name: Process as geometry
cadet: Each step of their process gets its own slowly rotating wireframe shape. On phones, they swap to lightweight flat drawings.
why: It explains a technical process visually and signals precision without a paragraph of copy.
engineer: Wireframe platonic solids rendered in Three.js, animated only while on screen. Below the mobile breakpoint the canvas is hidden and a 150px [[SVG]] takes its place.

name: Breakout split-text
cadet: A big statement breaks apart and reassembles line by line as you scroll.
why: It slows the reader down on the one sentence that matters.
engineer: One master controller owns the split-text, scroll-section and fade-up behaviors, so they share a single [[ScrollTrigger]] setup instead of fighting each other.

name: Pinned video gallery
cadet: The page holds still while a gallery of installation videos plays through, then lets go.
why: Video is their strongest proof, so it gets the whole screen.
engineer: HLS video loads eagerly and autoplays muted. The scroll distance lives in the Designer on a runway element per breakpoint, so the animation and the pin end at the same moment.

name: Dot-field text mask
cadet: A field of dots reacts to your cursor, and the headline is cut out of it.
why: It turns the call to action into something people play with.
engineer: The dot spacing is set per breakpoint with data attributes (desktop, tablet, mobile), read by a helper that rebuilds the grid when the window crosses a breakpoint.

name: WebGL atmosphere
cadet: Soft, moving light effects sit behind the footer and gallery, like light spill from a screen.
why: The site feels lit, the way their installations are.
engineer: Five [[Unicorn Studio]] scenes, initialised once globally. A second init call would break every embed, so it is guarded.

name: Case-results map
cadet: A dotted map of the U.S. shows real case wins. Filter by type, hover a pin for a quick summary, click it for the whole story. The firm adds a case in the CMS and a new pin appears.
why: Instead of claiming "we serve families nationwide", the page shows it.
engineer: A [[D3]] orthographic projection draws the map from us-atlas [[TopoJSON]]. Pins are read from a hidden CMS list; nearby pins cluster. Popups use cream glass and are portaled to a fixed layer so the map's clipping can't cut them off.

name: Cream-glass design language
cadet: Cards, menus and popups look like frosted glass tinted warm cream, with a thin gold line on top.
why: It feels calm and premium, and gives the firm a look nobody else in their market has.
engineer: Cream at 55–96% opacity with backdrop-filter blur(20px) saturate(1.6), a white hairline, layered navy shadows and a tan accent rule. Every rule ships the -webkit- prefix, or Safari shows a solid slab.

name: Morphing navigation
cadet: The menu starts full width over the hero, then shrinks into a floating pill as you scroll, and hides while you read.
why: Twenty-plus pages stay one click away without the menu getting in the way.
engineer: A scroll observer toggles condensed and hidden states. Pages without a hero start as the pill. The two-tier structure was approved by the attorney before build.

name: English / Spanish
cadet: The whole team is bilingual, so the site is too. One toggle switches the language.
why: Many clients are Spanish-speaking families. Neither language is an afterthought.
engineer: Copy ships in both languages and a toggle swaps them in place, remembering the choice.

name: Connected content system
cadet: A 58-term vocabulary, practice-area pages and articles all link to each other, so both people and search engines can follow a topic.
why: The firm shows up for the questions clients actually ask.
engineer: Topics, Insights and Practice Areas are cross-referenced collections. Category hubs and a vocabulary hub are generated from the same references, so a new term is linked everywhere automatically.

name: The orbit mark
cadet: A ring with a gap and a small square in orbit around it. The gap is where the square is "launching" from.
why: It says gravity and motion without drawing a rocket.
engineer: Three circles on a 1 : 0.618 : 0.382 ratio set the ring, the square's orbit and the gap. Stroke width is 12 on a 200 grid, so it survives down to 16px.
snippet:
<svg viewBox="-120 -120 240 240">
  <!-- a 3/4 ring on the golden circle (r 61.8) -->
  <path d="M 0 -61.8 A 61.8 61.8 0 1 0 61.8 0" fill="none" stroke-width="20"/>
  <!-- the square that orbits it -->
  <rect x="47" y="-15" width="30" height="30" fill="#FF6A3D"/>
</svg>

name: Square-first components
cadet: Every button and card has sharp corners. When you press a button, its shadow collapses like a key being pushed.
why: Sharp corners feel precise and technical, the opposite of soft template sites.
engineer: Radius token fixed at 0. Primary buttons carry a 4px offset shadow that collapses to 0 on press, with the label shifting 4px to match.

name: Type in three roles
cadet: A wide, heavy font for big headlines, a clean one for reading, and a "computer" font for small labels.
why: Each job gets the right voice, and the page reads like a design tool.
engineer: Archivo Expanded 900 (display), Geist (body), JetBrains Mono (labels, coordinates, sizes). Mono is reserved for things a design tool would print.
